summaries.summary: This extension is a malicious dropper. It obfuscates a URL, downloads a remote batch file to the user's Downloads folder, and executes it immediately. The execution is triggered on startup and on every text edit. The 'RESEARCH PURPOSE' description is a red herring; the code contains no legitimate functionality other than the payload delivery mechanism.

findings.description: The extension downloads a remote batch file (`update.bat`) from a hardcoded URL and executes it immediately using `child_process.exec`. This is a classic dropper pattern.
The extension claims to be for 'RESEARCH PURPOSE' but contains no research functionality. It only contains a payload downloader and executor. The advertised purpose is a decoy.

The URL is obfuscated using an array of characters and an index mapping to evade static signature detection. The decoded URL appears to be `https://1/23p.4:8` (likely a typo or specific C2 domain structure).
The malicious payload is triggered on every text document change (`onDidChangeTextDocument`), ensuring execution even if the user does not interact with the specific command.
Uses `curl -k` to disable SSL certificate verification, allowing man-in-the-middle attacks or execution of tampered payloads.
